Title: Why does IndexIVFPQFastScan support only 4-bits-per-index cases?
Description: # Summary

In the beginning of IndexIVFPQFastScan.cpp, it checks for `FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(nbits_per_idx == 4);`. It seems that FastScan shows better performance than normal IndexIVF search since it sorts QC with coarse list number beforehand. If this is the case, why is FastScan only applied to cases where it requires 4-bits per index? Is it also worth considering to apply this technique, sorting the queries beforehand based on coarse quantization results, to other cases, e.g., 8-bits-per-index cases, as well?
